title: Interaction of THIS_AND_FUTURE Delete and Edit with Existing Single-Instance Overrides

citations.verbatim_quote: The parameter specifies the effective range of recurrence instances that is specified by the property. The effective range is from the recurrence identifier specified by the property. If this parameter is not specified on an allowed property, then the default range is the single instance specified by the recurrence identifier value of the property. The parameter value can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the recurrence identifier and all subsequent instances.

The "RANGE" parameter is used to specify the effective range of recurrence instances from the instance specified by the "RECURRENCE-ID" property value. The value for the range parameter can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the given recurrence instance and all subsequent instances. Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time. Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

rationale: When a recurring series has one or more single-instance override components (`RECURRENCE-ID=rid, RRULE=None` per R-L2-005, or in legacy streams that also placed `rid` in the master component's `EXDATE`), two interactions arise when a subsequent operation targets `recurrence_id=split_rid` with `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range (either `delete` or `edit`): (Case A) `split_rid` itself was previously overridden as a single instance. Even if `split_rid` has a standalone override component (and even if a legacy stream also listed `split_rid` in the master component's `EXDATE`), `split_rid` is still the recurrence identifier of that slot in the recurring series; deleting or editing `THIS_AND_FUTURE` from `split_rid` MUST match and truncate/split the recurring master series at `split_rid` (not merely target the non-recurring override component) as well as removing the standalone override at `split_rid`. (Case B) Another standalone single-instance override exists for the same `UID` at `rid_future >= split_rid`. While RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 notes that in static iCalendar streams a `RANGE=THISANDFUTURE` override property does not implicitly reschedule separate override components, under a component-splitting `STORE_POLICY`, deleting all occurrences from `split_rid` onward (`THIS_AND_FUTURE` delete) MUST remove any standalone single-instance override components whose `RECURRENCE-ID` (resolved in the series timezone) is `>= split_rid` so that deleted future overrides do not remain orphaned on the calendar timeline. For a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit, whether those future overrides are removed or re-attached to the forked future segment is a separate store decision recorded as `split_future_override_mode`.
store_implication: When `delete` or `edit` is invoked with `recurrence_id=split_rid` and `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range: (1) Matching the recurring series: a recurring component (`RRULE` or `RDATE`) must match `split_rid` when `split_rid` is a candidate occurrence generated by its (dtstart, rrule, rdate) before its truncation bound, evaluated before EXDATE subtraction (so it matches even if a single-instance override component exists at `split_rid` or if a legacy stream also listed `split_rid` in `EXDATE`). (2) Overridden instances at or after `split_rid` (standalone overrides: `uid == target_uid`, `recurrence_id is not None`, and neither `rrule` nor `rdate` is present, compared by `RECURRENCE-ID` aligned to the series timezone, never by rescheduled `DTSTART`): a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` delete MUST remove every such override with `RECURRENCE-ID >= split_rid`; a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit handles them per `split_future_override_mode` (all removed under `DISCARD`). (3) Overrides with `RECURRENCE-ID < split_rid` MUST be left untouched by either operation.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Case A (Delete THIS_AND_FUTURE at an overridden occurrence): Daily series May 1..5 has May 3 overridden as a single instance (represented by a sibling RECURRENCE-ID=20250503T090000 component with exdate=[] on the master per R-L2-005, or with 2025-05-03T09:00:00 in master EXDATE in a legacy stream). Deleting 20250503T090000 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range must remove the May 3 override AND truncate the master RRULE UNTIL to 2025-05-03T08:59:59 so May 4 and May 5 are also deleted.

Case A (Edit THIS_AND_FUTURE at an overridden occurrence): If May 3 was overridden as a single instance, editing 20250503T090000 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range must fork a new recurring series from the recurring master (not from the non-recurring override which has RRULE=None) and truncate the master before May 3; under `split_future_override_mode=DISCARD` the old May 3 single-instance override is also removed.

Case B (Delete THIS_AND_FUTURE before a future override): Daily series May 1..5 has May 4 overridden as a single instance. Deleting 20250502T090000 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range must truncate the master before May 2 AND remove the standalone May 4 override component so only May 1 remains on the timeline (under every option of `split_future_override_mode`, since the future range is deleted).

Case B (Edit THIS_AND_FUTURE before a future override): editing 20250502T090000 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range when May 4 is overridden removes the May 4 override under `DISCARD`, or keeps it attached to the forked May 2.. segment (if May 4 is still a candidate of that segment) under `MIGRATE_TO_FUTURE_SERIES`.
Prior overrides strictly before split_rid (e.g. an override at May 2 when splitting THIS_AND_FUTURE at May 4) have RECURRENCE-ID < split_rid and MUST be preserved untouched.

As required by RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 ('Subsequent instances are determined by their RECURRENCE-ID value and not their current scheduled start time'), whether an existing override falls at or after the split boundary is determined by its RECURRENCE-ID, even if its rescheduled DTSTART was moved across the boundary.

scenarios.name: delete_this_and_future_at_previously_overridden_instance
scenarios.description: Deleting with THIS_AND_FUTURE range at an occurrence (May 3) that was previously edited as a single-instance override (with RECURRENCE-ID=20250503T090000 and exdate=[] on the master per R-L2-005) removes the May 3 override and truncates the master series so May 4 and May 5 are also removed.

scenarios.name: delete_this_and_future_purges_subsequent_standalone_override
scenarios.description: Deleting with THIS_AND_FUTURE range at May 2 when a standalone single-instance override exists at May 4 (with exdate=[] on the master per R-L2-005) truncates the master series before May 2 and removes the orphaned May 4 override component.

scenarios.name: delete_this_and_future_at_overridden_instance_with_legacy_master_exdate
scenarios.description: When a calendar stream contains both a RECURRENCE-ID override at May 3 and a legacy EXDATE for May 3 on the master component, deleting May 3 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range still matches the master component's unexcluded recurrence rule, truncates the master series before May 3, prunes the out-of-range EXDATE, and removes the May 3 override.

audit_notes: Scrubbed all references to internal files and methods to enforce 100% clean-room specification.
Contextual RFC check (+/- 40 lines): Verified RFC 5545 Section 3.2.13 (L1323-L1330) and Section 3.8.4.4 (L6426-L6434).

Harmonized scenarios with R-L2-005 so standard single-instance overrides use RECURRENCE-ID with exdate=[] on the master component, while also preserving a dedicated scenario for legacy streams that included both EXDATE and RECURRENCE-ID.
